name: @topcoat-spike/dom-parity
description: The SSR-to-client hydration parity harness. Runs the real server HTML, the real bootstrap, the real pinned runtime and the real compiled island together under a live DOM, and measures what hydration does to the document.
$note-why-a-separate-package: contract/README.md records that the contract harness has NO jsdom, for two
reasons: jsdom 30 requires node ^24.15 (this environment is 24.5), and it
depends on parse5 8, which would put a second parse5 major next to the 7.3.0
the reference babel plugin parses templates with. The tree oracle must agree
with the plugin about HTML parsing, so a second parse5 in that tree is not
Both objections are about ONE dependency tree, not about jsdom. So this is a
separate package with its own node_modules and its own lockfile. Nothing in
contract/vendor changes, contract/vendor's parse5 stays the only parse5 the
oracle ever sees, and the parity harness -- which needs a live DOM and a real
MutationObserver, the whole point of it -- gets one.
jsdom is pinned to 29.1.1, the last line whose engines field admits node 24.5
install here. Verified: MutationObserver delivers characterData, childList and
$note-no-upstream-pin-of-its-own: The runtime under test is NOT taken from this package. It is read out of
contract/vendor/upstream/solid-js, the same hash-verified files demo-app's own
routes serve with include_str!. jsdom supplies the DOM and nothing else.
